definitions.explanation: The fundamental supporting structure of something, used figuratively for the core support of a family, organization, or system. Originally refers to the wooden frame of a festival float or stall.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{家|いえ}の{屋台骨|やたいぼね}だ。
examples.english: He is the backbone of the family.

examples.japanese: {会社|かいしゃ}の{屋台骨|やたいぼね}を{支|ささ}えているのはベテラン{社員|しゃいん}たちだ。
examples.english: It is the veteran employees who support the backbone of the company.

examples.japanese: {不況|ふきょう}で{国|くに}の{屋台骨|やたいぼね}が{揺|ゆ}らいでいる。
examples.english: The recession is shaking the very foundations of the country.

notes:
Originally refers to the wooden frame ({骨|ほね} = bone, frame) of an {屋台|やたい} (festival float or portable stall). Since this frame is what holds the entire structure together, the word came to mean the fundamental support of any organization or system.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {屋台骨|やたいぼね}を{支|ささ}える: to support the backbone/foundation
- {屋台骨|やたいぼね}が{揺|ゆ}らぐ: the foundation wavers
- {屋台骨|やたいぼね}が{傾|かたむ}く: the foundation tilts (i.e., is in trouble)
- {家|いえ}の{屋台骨|やたいぼね}: the pillar of the family

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {大黒柱|だいこくばしら}: main pillar, breadwinner — similar metaphor but specifically for the central pillar of a house
- {基盤|きばん}: foundation, base — more abstract and formal
- {礎|いしずえ}: cornerstone, foundation — more literary
